key_insight: Jailbreak uses LLM-assisted code synthesis to regenerate database storage readers that bypass JDBC/ODBC and read files directly into analytic-friendly columnar memory.
engineering_relevance: This could remove a major bottleneck in analytical pipelines by enabling direct ingestion from database storage into engines like DuckDB, Spark, and GPU-based frameworks.
method: Ingest database source code and documentation into an LLM to synthesize storage-decoding reader components.
Read PostgreSQL/MySQL storage files directly instead of routing through the database execution layer.
Materialize outputs as Apache Arrow buffers for downstream analytics engines.
evidence_signal: The authors validated correctness on TPC-H query results against JDBC/ODBC baselines and reported up to 27x end-to-end throughput speedups.
watch_item: Performance and correctness depend on accurately regenerating complex storage formats, so schema/version changes or undocumented format details could make readers brittle.
paper_title: Breaking Database Lock-in: Agentic Regeneration of High Performance Storage Readers for Database Bypass
